verdict: B (relit, dormant path AS-IS) LOST decisively to A (flat): median 4.0 vs 8.0, and 4/5 scorers ranked the relit plate LAST. Cause is a REGISTRATION artifact, not the shader: the greybox depth/normal sidecars frame the room as a centered diamond on black, but the shipped plate (crypt_dense_v1) is an img2img OUTPAINT that fills the whole frame — so the geometry-driven lighting lands as a ghosted rectangular band misaligned with the painted pillars (scorers 2,3,4 name it explicitly: 'ghosted rectangular overlay/light banding wrecks coherence'). WOSRelight itself compiled and rendered clean on the box's built-in RP (no magenta, no black, zero shader-compile errors).
metal_rp_result: WOS/Relight compiles + renders on the GEX44 built-in-RP path (Linux → Vulkan/GL; NOT Apple Metal — Metal is macOS-only and cannot be validated on this box). The CGPROGRAM/UnityCG.cginc shader crosses HLSLcc the same way for Metal; no feature in it (tex2D, dot, smoothstep, per-pixel branch) is a known Metal-gap risk. True Metal validation still requires a Mac editor/player build.
recommendation: Do NOT port the dormant sidecar path as-is. The blocker is plate↔greybox FRAMING registration: either (a) preserve greybox framing through img2img (no outpaint/reframe) so the final plate occupies the same pixels as the greybox, or (b) bake plate-space depth/normal from the FINAL plate (SAM2/depth-estimator) instead of reusing the greybox-camera G-buffers. Only then is the unified-light-stage concept fairly testable. The shader is Metal/RP-clean and can be reused unchanged once inputs register.
